constraints: The profile is owner-scoped to the user and must respect user_memory_controls (extract_after) and Space authority: do not synthesise a personal profile from Space-origin threads (see F-t3-060). ZDR turns never reach messages, so Dreaming cannot see them, and prompt caching is disabled outright under ZDR, so the stable-segment design must be ZDR-aware; persona text itself fires on ZDR turns by precedent. MemoryConsolidationWorkflow cannot be the vehicle: it is org-scoped, registered DeniesZDR, and capability-core hard-rejects scheduled fires of any workflow type other than InteractiveRunSupervision. Profiles must stay user-editable and provenance-labelled.
approachAdjustment: Build the profile writer as a second, slower pass in session-core's existing Dreaming loop (one bounded user-scope row per user, derived from accepted memories), not via the Temporal MemoryConsolidationWorkflow. For the cached prefix, split system content into a stable block (platform, org, persona, profile) and a per-turn dynamic block placed after the breakpoint, because today all system messages are joined into one string and per-turn memory in it defeats cross-turn cache hits. Slice into (1) profile writer plus stable segment (M), (2) tone presets plus timezone and locale via the resolver (S), (3) personal first-run step (S), (4) settings search and effective-privacy view (S, overlaps F-t3-068).
effortNote: M to L as a bundle: only the profile writer plus stable segment is M; presets, onboarding, settings search and effective privacy are separate small slices.
verdictReason: Memory extraction, the instruction resolver, persona, a verbosity setting and typed settings actions already exist, so the item overstates the gap; its proposed vehicle (MemoryConsolidationWorkflow on a schedule) cannot work and the cache change needs a system-block split, not just a new block.

constraints: Space scope must be authorised per turn by a Control-signed decision and fail closed; session-core must not decide Space membership itself. Space-scoped rows need Space-deletion and erasure coverage including semantic copies. The semantic tier supports only equality filters, so 'active scope plus allowed parents' must be composed in session-core Postgres or by multiple queries, not by a tag filter. External semantic indexing is suppressed for ZDR-waived runs. Agent memory must never carry authority or widen access, and the unique index must include scope_id.
approachAdjustment: Reorder: (1) S fail-closed fix first: exclude Space-origin and agent_run threads from user-scope extraction and Space turns from user-scope recall until a Space scope exists, with a regression test; (2) M Space scope (scope='space' plus scope_id) read and written only on turns carrying a Control-signed Space decision, reusing the source_scope isolation pattern; (3) Project scope waits for server Projects (I21) and should be considered as a mapping onto Spaces rather than a new entity; (4) agent scope last, once agent runs read it (agent runs use the save_memory and recall_memory tools keyed to the user today).

verdictReason: Gap is real and the baseline 'Space memory not verified' is now resolved as absent, but the code shows an immediate fail-closed leak risk (Space threads feed and are recalled from personal memory) that should lead, and the semantic tier cannot express parent-scope filters.
